title: 47 Suvarnabhumi flights cancelled over Middle East unrest
detail: Khaosod English reported 47 cancellations at Suvarnabhumi on 2 March and 108 between 28 Feb and 2 Mar, by eight airlines, attributed to Middle East unrest; the airport said no passengers were stranded.
attribution: Per Suvarnabhumi Airport via Khaosod English

title: Phuket runway closed after hard landing; 165 flights hit
detail: The Nation reported an Air India Express hard landing disabled the aircraft and closed Phuket's runway until a targeted 21:00 reopening; AOT said 165 flights across four airports were affected.
attribution: Flight figures per AOT via The Nation

title: Planned MEA power cuts in east Bangkok and Nonthaburi
detail: Thairath English relayed an MEA notice of planned maintenance outages on Suwinthawong Road, Bangkok (8:30–15:30) and Rattanathibet Road, Nonthaburi (8:00–14:00).
attribution: Planned outage per MEA notice via Thairath

title: Battery truck fire damages Burapha Withi Expressway
detail: An InterRisk Asia review said a truck carrying lithium-ion batteries caught fire and exploded near km 40 of Highway 34, with the heat damaging the elevated Burapha Withi Expressway above; no deaths were reported.
place: Theparat Road (Highway 34) near km 40, under Burapha Withi Expressway

title: Chao Phraya Dam release to rise; 7 provinces warned
detail: The Nation reported Regional Irrigation Office 12 planned discharge of 500–700 m3/s, raising downstream levels about 1–1.5 m while staying below banks.
attribution: Per RID Regional Irrigation Office 12 via The Nation

title: Heavy-rain warning; national reservoirs at 56%
detail: The Nation reported TMD warned of heavy rain 8–14 June; officials said national reservoirs held 56% and the four main Chao Phraya dams 53% of capacity.
attribution: Storage figures per officials via The Nation

title: Planned MEA power cuts in Bangkok and Samut Prakan
detail: Thairath English relayed an MEA notice of maintenance and undergrounding outages at several Bangkok sites and one in Samut Prakan, mostly between 8:30 and 15:30.
place: Multiple sites incl. Chalerm Phrakiat R.9 Soi 28, Sukhumvit Soi 62
attribution: Planned outage per MEA notice via Thairath

title: RID warns 7 provinces of higher Chao Phraya Dam flow
detail: The Nation reported RID expected dam discharge to rise to 500–700 m3/s, lifting downstream levels about 1–1.5 m, with 936 m3/s measured at station C.2.

title: Suvarnabhumi postpones 7-month terminal road lane closures
detail: The Nation reported Suvarnabhumi cancelled lane closures on its elevated terminal road, planned for 31 Aug 2026–7 Apr 2027 for expansion-joint repairs, after criticism over high-season timing; a new schedule is pending.
attribution: Per Suvarnabhumi Airport via The Nation

title: Internet connectivity drop detected in Pathum Thani (low confidence)
detail: Voidly logged an IODA-detected connectivity drop in the Pathum Thani region from 12:30 UTC; it rated confidence moderate and corroboration low, with no networks named.

title: Planned MEA power cuts across Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Samut Prakan
detail: Thairath English relayed an MEA notice of planned outages at 12 locations for maintenance and undergrounding, including one overnight Bangkok outage to 01:30 on 17 September.
place: Multiple sites incl. Ramkhamhaeng, Phahonyothin, Bang Pu
attribution: Planned outage per MEA notice via Thairath

title: RID flood alert for 11 Chao Phraya basin provinces
detail: The Nation reported RID planned Chao Phraya Dam discharge of 700–1,000 m3/s, with levels up 0.6–1.5 m and Ayutthaya areas outside embankments most at risk.

title: Chao Phraya Dam release raised to 1,000–1,300 m3/s
detail: The Nation reported RID would raise discharge from about 990 to 1,000–1,300 m3/s after heavy northern rain, warning of a 0.5–1.5 m rise downstream.

title: DDPM puts 10 provinces on watch as Chao Phraya rises
detail: Chiang Rai Times reported DDPM alerted 10 central provinces including Bangkok, citing Chao Phraya Dam releases of 700–1,000 m3/s and Ayutthaya's Sena, Bang Ban and Bang Pa-in as high-risk.
agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation
attribution: Per DDPM via Chiang Rai Times

title: RID to raise Chao Phraya Dam release to 1,500–2,000 m3/s
detail: The Nation reported RID planned releases of 1,500–2,000 m3/s ahead of heavy rain on 23–27 Sept, warning 11 provinces and of rises of 0.7–1.7 m outside embankments in Ayutthaya and Ang Thong.
